concerns.concern: The theory models a 2H bilayer of mutually inverted layers, where interlayer hopping restores inversion. In the actual misfit crystal all 1H layers have the same orientation, so interlayer hopping would not restore inversion and the proposed 'decoupling → mixing' mechanism is not the relevant control parameter.
concerns.quote: With same-orientation stacking, finite t⊥ would not restore inversion, so the proposed mechanism ("decoupling → mixing") is not the relevant control parameter for this material.

concerns.concern: No microscopic evidence ties the two gaps to specific momenta or to triplet content. The authors' own theory admits a conventional singlet-only multiband explanation, and the only discriminant offered (interlayer hopping) is never varied in the study.
concerns.quote: The only discriminant offered is the t⊥-dependence, and t⊥ is not varied within this study.

concerns.concern: Experiments that could distinguish mixed-parity from conventional multiband pairing are missing: quasiparticle interference to assign gaps to pockets, temperature dependence of both gaps, disorder sensitivity, and field-dependent filling of the two gaps.
concerns.quote: Experiments that would actually distinguish the scenarios are absent

concerns.concern: The claim of intrinsic superconductivity in the SnS layer is contradicted by the authors' data. A similar gap magnitude, the same critical field, comparable coherence lengths and a single bulk transition all point to tunneling into TaS2 or a proximitized layer.
concerns.quote: The claim of intrinsic superconductivity in the SnS layer is not supported and is contradicted by the authors' own data.

concerns.concern: Charge transfer from SnS to TaS2 is ignored. It could by itself explain the Tc enhancement and the modified gap structure, independently of interlayer hopping. ARPES Fermi-surface volumes compared with 2H and monolayer TaS2 are needed.
concerns.quote: Charge transfer is a ubiquitous and dominant effect in misfit compounds.

concerns.concern: The single-gap versus two-gap fit comparison is unfair. The single-gap fit uses an isotropic BCS form with an unusually high 900 mK effective temperature, and no equally parameterized alternatives (Dynes, anisotropic single gap, Γ/K isotropic s-wave) are compared, e.g. via information criteria.
concerns.quote: The single-gap fit (SM Fig. 2) uses an isotropic BCS form with an unusually high effective temperature (900 mK).

concerns.concern: Novelty is overstated. Ising superconductivity and decoupling in misfit TMDs, two gaps of the same magnitude in exfoliated monolayer TaS2, and singlet–triplet mixing in 1H layers are all already known.
concerns.quote: Novelty is more limited than presented.

concerns.concern: Decoupling is supported only indirectly. Opposite spin polarization at K/K′ would appear in a same-orientation stack even with appreciable interlayer coupling.
concerns.quote: Spin polarization at K/K′ would appear in a same-orientation stack even with appreciable interlayer coupling

concerns.concern: The kz-independence is shown only for EDCs near a single M point. There is no kz Fermi-surface map and no quantitative upper bound on interlayer hopping.
concerns.quote: The kz-independence is shown only for EDCs at a single M-point region, without a Fermi-surface kz map or an estimate of an upper bound on t⊥.

concerns.concern: The supporting correlation across monolayer, 4Hb, misfit and 2H TaS2 is not a controlled test. These materials differ in doping, CDW state, disorder and substrate, and the 4Hb 'destroyed second gap' interpretation is itself contested.
concerns.quote: compares materials that differ in doping, CDW state, disorder, and substrate.

concerns.concern: The theory disagrees quantitatively with experiment: the computed small/large gap ratio is ~0.1 versus ~0.6 measured.
concerns.quote: The computed small/large gap ratio on the K pockets is ~0.1 (SM), versus ~0.6 experimentally.

concerns.concern: The computed gap scale (~5 meV) is about ten times larger than the measured gaps.
concerns.quote: The computed gap scale (~0.02 t ≈ 5 meV) is ~10× larger than measured.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 5e inset shows the triplet-to-singlet weight ratio at or below 0.3, contradicting the claim that the weights are comparable.
concerns.quote: The inset of Fig. 5e shows εA2u/εA1g ≤ 0.3. This contradicts the narrative that the weights are "comparable".

concerns.concern: The interaction parameters are chosen ad hoc, and no phase diagram shows how generic the two-gap regime is.
concerns.quote: The interaction parameters (V0 = 0.25t, V1 = V2 = 0.3t) are chosen ad hoc, with no phase diagram showing how generic the two-gap regime is.

concerns.concern: The claimed role of on-site Coulomb repulsion in enhancing the triplet component is asserted but not demonstrated in the model.
concerns.quote: The asserted role of on-site Coulomb repulsion in enhancing the triplet component is stated but not shown.

concerns.concern: The model is single-orbital with a coarse 40×40 k-mesh and a 1 meV Dynes broadening comparable to or larger than the experimental gaps, raising doubts about whether the features are resolved.
concerns.quote: That broadening is comparable to or larger than the experimental gaps, which raises questions about resolving the features.

concerns.concern: The theory should state clear predictions that distinguish mixed-parity A1g/A2u pairing from A1g-only multiband pairing, such as in-plane Hc2 beyond the Ising limit, disorder sensitivity, and gap-anisotropy patterns.
concerns.quote: State clear predictions that distinguish A1g/A2u mixing from A1g-only multiband pairing

concerns.concern: The dirty two-band (Gurevich-type) Hc2 model is an orbital-limit model and is physically inappropriate for the in-plane field of an Ising, Pauli-protected 2D superconductor. Its near-Tc behavior is generic to such systems anyway.
concerns.quote: Applying it to the in-plane field of an Ising, Pauli-protected 2D superconductor is physically inappropriate.

concerns.concern: The Hc2 fits return different coupling constants for the two field orientations, which is unphysical because intrinsic couplings cannot depend on field direction.
concerns.quote: Intrinsic couplings cannot depend on field direction, so the fits are not mutually consistent.

concerns.concern: The Hc2 fits converge to symmetric bands (λ11 = λ22), undercutting their use as evidence for two distinct gaps.
concerns.quote: The fits converge to λ11 = λ22, i.e., symmetric bands, which undercuts their use as evidence for two distinct gaps.

concerns.concern: Comparing the SnS termination with the 1T termination of 4Hb-TaS2 is not apt, because 1T-TaS2 is a correlated Mott/CDW insulator with very different tunneling and proximity physics.
concerns.quote: Comparison with the 1T termination of 4Hb-TaS2 is not apt

concerns.concern: The absence of a second gap on SnS may simply reflect momentum-selective tunneling or a different matrix element, rather than a distinct condensate.
concerns.quote: The "absence of a second gap" may simply reflect momentum-selective tunneling or a different matrix element.

concerns.concern: The Fermi-surface-mismatch argument borrowed from Ref. 78 assumes interface parameters that are not established for this system.
concerns.quote: Ref. 78's Fermi-surface-mismatch argument assumes specific interface parameters not established here.

concerns.concern: The internal-pressure explanation for SnS superconductivity would require more than 40 GPa-equivalent compression, with no structural or DFT support offered.
concerns.quote: The "internal pressure" hypothesis would need >40 GPa-equivalent compression, for which no structural or DFT support is offered.

concerns.concern: Vortex imaging on SnS does not prove intrinsic superconductivity, since proximitized layers or tunneling through a layer into a superconductor also show vortices. Temperature-dependent, thickness-dependent and setpoint-dependent STS and DFT/ARPES of SnS states at EF are needed, or the gap should be presented as induced.
concerns.quote: A proximitized layer, or a layer through which one tunnels into a superconductor, also displays vortices.

concerns.concern: The stated agreement of the 3 kG STM critical field with transport is inconsistent with Fig. 2b, which shows Hc2∥c of about 0.5–0.6 T at 0.4–0.5 K.
concerns.quote: inconsistent with Fig. 2b, which shows Hc2∥c ≈ 0.5–0.6 T at ~0.4–0.5 K.

concerns.concern: Coherence-length values are internally inconsistent across the main text, the SM and the Hc2 estimate.
concerns.quote: 35 ± 5 nm in the main text, 45 ± 10 nm in the SM, and ~30 nm from Hc2.

concerns.concern: The two-gap fit parameters (weights, effective temperature, broadening) and the lock-in modulation amplitude are not reported. The effective electron temperature should be calibrated, e.g. on a reference superconductor; without this the ~300 µeV kink cannot be judged.
concerns.quote: The two-gap fit parameters (N1/N2 weights, Teff, broadening) and the lock-in modulation amplitude used for the gap spectra are not reported.

concerns.concern: The magnitude and units of the spin polarization are unclear: ±0.5 labeled as percent is either a mislabeled fraction or an extremely small polarization.
concerns.quote: The claimed polarization scale ("P [%]" of ±0.5) is either a mislabeled fraction or an extremely small polarization

concerns.concern: The CDW seen in STM but absent in resistivity is not reconciled.
concerns.quote: Reconcile the CDW seen in STM with its absence in transport.

concerns.concern: Eq. (9) writes the antisymmetric gap with the symmetric interaction V(s) instead of V(a).
concerns.quote: In Eq. (9), Δ(a) is written with V(s) instead of V(a).

concerns.concern: Interlayer-hopping values are inconsistent between the main text and the SM, and SM figures are mislabeled 't = 0' for t⊥.
concerns.quote: the main text uses t⊥/λ = 2 and a merger at 0.8λ, while the SM uses 0.1 and 0.2 eV

concerns.concern: The fitted residual resistivity (145 µΩcm) contradicts the plotted value of about 30 µΩcm.
concerns.quote: The fitted residual resistivity (145 µΩcm) contradicts the plotted ~30 µΩcm.

concerns.concern: The fitted saturation resistivity is about 60 times the 300 K value, so it cannot produce visible saturation.
concerns.quote: The saturation resistivity (23 mΩcm) is ~60× the 300 K value, so it cannot cause visible saturation.

concerns.concern: The resistivity fit prefactor C is unconstrained by the fit, with an error larger than its value.
concerns.quote: The prefactor C = 3.7 ± 5 mΩcm is unconstrained.

concerns.concern: The Bloch–Grüneisen integrand contains a typo.
concerns.quote: The Bloch–Grüneisen integrand contains a typo, (1−e⁻¹) instead of (1−e⁻ˣ).

concerns.concern: Tc is quoted inconsistently throughout the manuscript.
concerns.quote: Tc is quoted variously as 3.05, 3.1, and 3.14 K.

concerns.concern: The lock-in frequency differs between the figure captions and the Methods.
concerns.quote: 870 Hz in the captions versus 907 Hz in Methods.

concerns.concern: There are references to non-existent figure panels, including the Fig. 5 caption citing 'panel (b)' for the DOS.
concerns.quote: There are references to non-existent panels ("Fig. 2c"; "Fig. 1c/1e" for STM data).

concerns.concern: The Discussion says 'strongly coupled case' where 'weakly coupled' is meant.
concerns.quote: the f-wave component is large in the "strongly coupled case" when "weakly coupled" is meant.

concerns.concern: The SM section on magnetic-field dependence is empty.
concerns.quote: The SM section on magnetic-field dependence is empty.
